hints.title: Ordered Traversal Sequence
hints.text: Sorting all node values takes extra time and space. What traversal order visits the values of an ordered binary tree in strictly increasing sequence?

hints.title: In-Order Ascending Invariant
hints.text: An in-order traversal (left child, current node, right child) visits nodes in strictly ascending sorted order. The kth node visited is the answer.

hints.title: Early Stopping In-Order Procedure
hints.text: Traverse in-order iteratively or recursively while decrementing a counter k for each visited node. When k reaches 0, the current node value is the answer, so stop further traversal and return it.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: tree height (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Terminates immediately upon popping the kth smallest element from the in-order stack.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting all nodes into an array and sorting takes O(N log N) time and O(N) space, ignoring the sorted BST structure.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stopping in-order traversal as soon as k elements are visited takes O(H + k) time and O(H) space, avoiding traversing the remainder of the tree.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Halting traversal immediately upon reaching the kth element, iterative stack or clean stateful traversal, and discussion of augmenting nodes with subtree sizes for frequent queries.

solutions.approach: Iterative In-Order Stack with Early Exit
